subject: CrystalView: Proof-of-Value sprint — proposed success metrics & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@crystalview.ai>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@crystalview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CrystalView: Proof-of-Value sprint — proposed success metrics & next steps

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a suggested 3-week Proof-of-Value (PoV) sprint so we keep momentum. Please confirm the success criteria and any constraints below so we can lock owners and dates.

Summary of what we heard you want to validate:
- Accuracy: <= 12% false positives on anomaly detection over a held-out sample (you suggested balanced labels)
- Latency: median inference latency < 120ms for 512-token requests under typical load
- Cost target: per-inference cost that is competitive with your current provider (we should baseline after first week)
- Integration: end-to-end embedding + reranking integrated into your search UI with feature parity for A/B testing

Proposed PoV plan (high level)
1) Week 0 (kickoff) — environment access, sample dataset, success-metric confirmation, security check
2) Week 1 — model onboarding, baseline runs, initial latency/cost numbers
3) Week 2 — tuning (batching/quantization), embed+rerank integration, end-to-end validation
4) Week 3 — readout, handoff to your SRE/engineering for roll-forward or next steps

Owners (proposed)
- Redwood POC lead: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.ai) — implementation, infra, model tuning
- Customer success / onboarding: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.ai) — runbooks, training, acceptance criteria checklist
- CrystalView technical lead: Alyssa (please confirm) — data access and evaluation set validity

Immediate asks for kickoff: please share
- A short sample of the dataset (<= 50MB) and a schema description
- A list of any required security controls or redlines (SOC2, retention limits)
- A primary kickoff date window (we propose July 12–15)

I attached a draft PoV runbook (redwood_pov_runbook_v1.pdf) to show the checklist we run through. I’ll open a HubSpot deal and a shared Drive folder for artifacts once you confirm.

If this looks good I’ll lock the kickoff calendar invite and loop in our infra engineer.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0191

Attachment: redwood_pov_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 480KB)
From: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@crystalview.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrystalView: Proof-of-Value sprint — proposed success metrics & next steps

Thanks Rishi — great summary and aligned on the goals. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success metrics: we can accept the accuracy and latency targets as a starting point, but need a secondary metric: stability under burst (95th percentile latency under traffic surge). Can you include that in the baseline reporting?
- Legal & security: procurement/legal asked for our standard questionnaire; I’ve attached the latest security checklist we use (crystalview_security_q1.pdf). We’ll need a SOC 2 attestation and confirmation on data retention policies during the PoV.
- Data: we can share a de-identified sample; engineering will confirm schema and S3 access by Monday (Jul 5).
- Kickoff: July 12 works for a 60-minute kickoff — we prefer mornings (PST).

One ask from our CTO: if you can provide a short note on what logs/artifacts Redwood will collect during the PoV (we want minimal PII and only operational telemetry). Also can you confirm whether model weights will stay in your hosted environment or if you require us to open a VPC for Private mode testing?

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Gomez
Director of ML Engineering | CrystalView AI
alyssa@crystalview.ai

Attachment: crystalview_security_q1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@crystalview.ai>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@crystalview.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrystalView: Proof-of-Value sprint — proposed success metrics & next steps

Great — thanks for the clarifications and the security checklist, Alyssa. Quick responses and owners below so we’re ready for the July 12 kickoff: 

- Stability metric: yes, Ben will add 95th percentile burst testing to the baseline report.
- Logs/artifacts: Redwood will collect only operational telemetry and aggregated model metrics (latency, token counts, error rates). We will not collect request payloads containing PII. Full list will be included in the runbook.
- Deployment mode: for this PoV we propose running on Redwood Hosted with customer data kept in your S3 bucket (we pull only the sample via temporary credentials). If you prefer a VPC/private test, we can enable Redwood Private but that will add ~3 business days for network setup — let us know preference.

Confirmed owners
- PoV implementation lead (Redwood): Ben Carter — ben@redwood.ai — will be your day-to-day for infra and tuning
- PoV onboarding & acceptance (Redwood): Marissa Cole — marissa@redwood.ai — will own the success checklist and readout
- Customer technical lead: Alyssa Gomez — please confirm additional CrystalView attendees (SRE/CTO) for kickoff

Next steps before July 12 (action items)
- Alyssa / CrystalView: share de-identified sample data + schema by Mon Jul 5 (OPEN)
- CrystalView legal: confirm SOC2 attestation and retention constraints (OPEN)
- Redwood: create Drive folder + HubSpot deal, share PoV runbook and kickoff invite (IN PROGRESS)

Links/Artifacts
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/2417
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cX-redwood-crystalview-pov
- PoV runbook attached to earlier email (redwood_pov_runbook_v1.pdf)

I’ll send the calendar invite for July 12 shortly and copy the Redwood infra engineer (to be confirmed).

Best,
Rishi
